The channel from Dianshan Lake into the Huangpu is growing shallow with silt and should be dredged. From the Huangpu, Henglao, and Zhujing, through Xiuzhou Canal into the South Mo, down to Shanjing Harbor—a stretch of more than fourteen thousand zhang urgently needing dredging.
75
他如蘇之茜涇、楊林、白茆、七浦諸港，鬆之蒲匯、官紹諸塘，常、鎮之澡港、九曲諸河，並宜設法開導，次第修舉。」
The same holds for Suzhou's Qianjing, Yanglin, Baimao, and Qipu harbors; Songjiang's Puhui and Guanshao canals; and Changzhou and Zhenjiang's Zaogang and Jiuqu rivers—each should be opened by proper methods and repaired in turn."
76
八年，又言：「蘇、鬆諸郡幹河支港凡數百，大則泄水入海，次則通湖達江，小則引流灌田。 今吳淞江、白茆塘、秀州塘、蒲匯塘、孟瀆河、舜河、青暘港俱已告成，支河數十，宜盡開浚。 」俱從其請。
In year eight he again reported, "Suzhou and Songjiang have hundreds of trunk channels and branch waterways—large ones discharge to the sea, middling ones link lakes to rivers, small ones carry water to the fields. The Wusong, Baimao Canal, Xiuzhou Canal, Puhui Canal, Mengdu River, Shun River, and Qingyang Harbor are now finished; dozens of branch streams should all be dredged open. All was approved.
77
久之，用儀望議，特設蘇、鬆水利副使，以許應逵領之。 乃浚吳淞八十餘晨，築塘九十餘處，開新河百二十三道，浚內河百三十九道，築上海李家洪老鴉嘴海岸十八里，發帑金二十萬。 應逵以其半訖工。 三十七、八年間，霪雨浸溢，水患日熾。 越數年，給事中歸子顧言：「宋時，吳淞江闊九里。 元末淤塞。 正統間，周忱立表江心，疏而浚之。 崔恭、徐貫、李充嗣、海瑞相繼浚者凡五，迄今四十餘年，廢而不講。 宜使江闊水駛，塘浦支河分流四達。 」疏入留中。 巡按御史薛貞復請行之，下部議而未行。 至天啟中，巡撫都御史周起元復請浚吳淞、白茆。 崇禎初，員外郎蔡懋德、巡撫都御史李待問皆以為請。 久之，巡撫都御史張國維請疏吳江長橋七十二谼及九里、石塘諸洞。 御史李謨復請浚吳淞、白茆。 俱下部議，未能行也。
Later, on Yi Wang's recommendation, a special vice commissioner for Suzhou and Songjiang hydraulic works was created, with Xu Yingkui in charge. He dredged more than eighty zhang of the Wusong, built embankments at ninety-plus sites, cut one hundred twenty-three new channels and cleared one hundred thirty-nine inner waterways, raised eighteen li of coast at Shanghai's Lijiahong and Laoyazui, and disbursed two hundred thousand taels from the treasury. Yingkui brought the work to completion with half that sum. In years thirty-seven and thirty-eight, unending rain brought floods, and the water crisis grew worse by the day. Several years on, supervising secretary Gui Ziguan memorialized, "Under the Song the Wusong was nine li wide. By the late Yuan it had silted shut. In the Zhengtong reign Zhou Chen set a gauge midstream and dredged it clear. Cui Gong, Xu Guan, Li Chongsi, and Hai Rui undertook dredging in turn—five efforts in all—yet for more than forty years since, the work has lain neglected. The river should be widened and the current quickened, with canal embankments and branch streams branching flow in every direction. The memorial was filed and held over at court. Investigating censor Xue Zhen petitioned again for implementation; the ministries debated it, but nothing was done. In the Tianqi reign, grand coordinator Zhou Qiyuan again urged dredging the Wusong and Baimao. Early in Chongzhen, vice director Cai Maode and grand coordinator Li Daiwen both pressed the same plea. Later, grand coordinator Zhang Guowei asked to clear Wujiang's seventy-two gorges at Chang Bridge plus the culverts at Jiuli and Shitang. Censor Li Mo again urged dredging the Wusong and Baimao. Each proposal went to the ministries for debate, and none could be implemented.
78
十年，增築雄縣橫堤八里，禦滹沱暴漲。
In year ten, Xiongxian's transverse dike was extended eight li to hold back the Hutuo in flood.
79
十三年，以尚寶少卿徐貞明兼御史，領墾田使。 貞明為給事中，嘗請興西北水利如南人圩田之制，引水成田。 工部覆議：「畿輔諸郡邑，以上流十五河之水泄於貓兒一灣，海口又極束隘，故所在橫流。 必多開支河，挑浚海口，而後水勢可平，疏浚可施。 然役大費繁，而今以民勞財匱，方務省事，請罷其議。 」乃已。 後貞明謫官，著《潞水客譚》一書，論水利當興者十四條。 時巡撫張國彥、副使顧養謙方開水利於薊、永有效，於是給事中王敬民薦貞明，特召還，賜敕勘水利。 貞明乃先治京東州邑，如密雲燕樂莊，平谷水峪寺、龍家務莊，三河塘會莊、順慶屯地。 薊州城北黃厓營，城西白馬泉、鎮國莊，城東馬伸橋，夾林河而下別山鋪，夾陰流河而下至於陰流。 遵化平安城，夾運河而下沙河鋪西，城南鐵廠、湧珠湖以下韭菜溝、上素河、下素河百餘里。 豐潤之南，則大寨、剌榆坨、史家河、大王莊，東則榛子鎮，西則鴉紅橋，夾河五十餘里。 玉田青莊塢、後湖莊、三里屯及大泉、小泉，至於瀕海之地，自水道沽關、黑嚴子墩至開平衛南宋家營，東西百餘里，南北百八十里。 墾田三萬九千餘畝。 至真定將治滹沱近堧地，御史王之棟言：「滹沱非人力可治，徒耗財擾民。 」帝入其言，欲罪諸建議者。 申時行言：「墾田興利謂之害民，議甚舛。 顧為此說者，其故有二。 北方民遊惰好閑，憚於力作，水田有耕耨之勞，胼胝之苦，不便一也。 貴勢有力家侵佔甚多，不待耕作，坐收蘆葦薪芻之利； 若開墾成田，歸於業戶，隸於有司，則已利盡失，不便二也。 然以國家大計較之，不便者小，而便者大。 惟在斟酌地勢，體察人情，沙堿不必盡開，黍麥無煩改作，應用伕役，必官募之，不拂民情，不失地利，乃謀國長策耳。 」於是貞明得無罪，而水田事終罷。
In year thirteen Xu Zhenming, Junior Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia, was also appointed investigating censor and put in charge of land reclamation. While still a supervising secretary, Zhenming had urged developing northwestern irrigation on the southern polder model, channeling water to make fields. The Ministry of Works replied, "In the metropolitan region, the waters of fifteen upstream rivers all empty into Maor Bay alone, while the estuary is desperately narrow—so floods spread everywhere. Branch channels must be opened and the estuary dredged before the waters can level off and ordinary dredging can succeed. But the labor would be vast and costly, and with the people exhausted and the treasury bare the court was bent on retrenchment—so they asked that the plan be dropped. And so it ended. Later, after Zhenming was demoted, he wrote *Visitor's Talk on Lu River Water*, setting out fourteen proposals for waterworks that ought to be revived. Grand coordinator Zhang Guoyan and vice commissioner Gu Yangqian were then opening works in Ji and Yong with good effect; supervising secretary Wang Jingmin recommended Zhenming, who was specially recalled and charged by edict to survey hydraulic works. Zhenming began in the eastern capital districts—Miyun's Yanle Manor; Pinggu's Shuiyu Temple and Longjiawu Manor; Sanhe's Tanghui Manor and Shunqing garrison lands. North of Jizhou stood Huangya Camp; west of the city, Baima Spring and Zhenguo Manor; east of the city, Mashen Bridge; along the Lin River down to Bieshan Post; along the Yinliu River down to Yinliu. At Zunhua's Ping'an city, along the Grand Canal west of Shahe Post; south of the city, Tiechang and below Yongzhu Lake through Jiucai Gully, Upper Su River, and Lower Su River for more than one hundred li. South of Fengrun lay Dazhai, Ciyu Tuo, Shijia River, and Dawang Manor; to the east, Zhenzi Town; to the west, Yahong Bridge—more than fifty li along the river. Yutian's Qingzhuangwu, Houhuzhuang, Sanlitun, and the Great and Little Springs, down to the coast—from Shuidao Gu Pass and Heiyanzi Mound to Kaiping Guard's Southern Songjiaying: more than one hundred li east to west and one hundred eighty li north to south. They reclaimed more than thirty-nine thousand mu of fields. When he was about to tackle the Hutuo lowlands near Zhending, censor Wang Zhidong argued, "The Hutuo cannot be tamed by human effort; it would only waste money and trouble the people. The emperor took his view and meant to punish those who had urged the scheme. Shen Shixing said, "To call land reclamation and public benefit harmful to the people is perverse reasoning. Those who say so have two motives. First, northerners are lazy and shy from hard work; wet rice demands plowing, hoeing, and blistered hands—they find that inconvenient. Second, powerful families have seized vast tracts and, without farming, simply harvest reeds, rushes, and fodder. If the land were opened into fields, returned to farming households, and placed under officials, those easy profits would vanish. Yet weighed against the nation's larger interest, the inconveniences are small and the gains great. The long strategy is to read the terrain and the people: not every saline plot must be opened, nor every millet field turned to rice; labor should be hired by the state without trampling local custom or wasting the land's strengths. Zhenming was spared punishment, but the paddy-field program was abandoned in the end.
80
巡撫都御史樑問孟築橫城堡邊牆，慮寧夏有黃河患，請堤西岔河，障水東流。 從之。 十九年，尚寶丞周弘禴言：「寧夏河東有漢、秦二壩，請依河西漢、唐壩築以石，於渠外疏大渠一道，北達鴛鴦諸湖。 」詔可。
Grand coordinator Liang Wenmeng raised the border wall at Hengcheng Castle and, fearing Yellow River flooding in Ningxia, asked to dike the West Cha River to turn the current eastward. The request was approved. In year nineteen Junior Chamberlain Zhou Hongzuo reported, "East of the Ningxia River stand the Han and Qin dams; build them in stone like the Han and Tang dams on the west bank, and outside the canal cut a great channel north to Mandarin Duck and the other lakes. The emperor assented.
81
二十三年，黃、淮漲溢，淮、揚昏墊。 議者多請開高家堰以分淮。 寶應知縣陳煃為御史，慮高堰既開，害民產鹽場，請自興、鹽迤東，疏白塗河、石鵜達口、廖家港為數河，分門出海； 然後從下而上，浚清水、子嬰二溝，且多開瓜、儀閘口以泄水。 給事中祝世祿亦言：「議者欲放淮從廣陽、射陽二湖入海。 廣陽闊僅八里，射陽僅二十五丈，名為湖，實河也。 且離海三百里，迂迴淺窄，高、寶七州縣水惟此一線宣洩之，又使淮注焉，田廬鹽場，必無幸矣。 廣陽湖東有大湖，方廣六十里，湖北口有舊官河，自官蕩至鹽城石鵜達口，通海僅五十三里，此導淮入海一便也。 」下部及河漕官議，俱格不行。 既而總河尚書楊一魁言：「黃水倒灌，正以海口為阻。 分黃工就，則石鵜達口、廖家港、白駒場海口，金灣、芒稻諸河，急宜開刷。 」乃命如議行之。
In year twenty-three the Yellow and Huai flooded; Huai-Yang lay drowned under murky water. Most memorialists urged opening Gaojia Embankment to split the Huai. Baoying magistrate Chen Huang, now a censor, feared that opening Gaojia Embankment would ruin the people's salt pans; he asked that east from Xing and Yan the Baitu River, Shipu Dadao, and Liaojia Harbor be cleared as several outlets to the sea; then, working from downstream upward, clear the Qingshui and Ziying gullies and open more sluices at Guayi to discharge the flood. Supervising secretary Zhu Shilu also wrote, "Some propose to send the Huai out through Guangyang and Sheyang lakes into the sea. Guangyang is only eight li across; Sheyang only twenty-five zhang—they are called lakes but are really rivers. They lie three hundred li from the sea, winding, shallow, and narrow—the seven prefectures and counties of Gaoyou and Baoying have only this single outlet; pour the Huai into it and fields, homes, and salt pans would be doomed. East of Guangyang Lake lies a great lake sixty li square; north of its mouth runs an old official channel from Guandang to Yancheng's Shipu Dadao—only fifty-three li to the sea—an easy route for the Huai to reach the ocean. The proposal went to the ministries and river-transport offices for debate, but every line was blocked and nothing was done. Director-General of Rivers Yang Yikui then argued, "The Yellow River backs up because the estuary is choked. Once the Yellow River diversion is done, Shipu Dadao, Liaojia Harbor, the Baiju Chang estuary, Jinwan, Mangdao, and the other channels must be opened and scoured at once. An order followed to implement the plan.
82
三十年，保定巡撫都御史汪應蛟言：「易水可溉金臺，滹水可溉恆山，溏水可溉中山，滏水可溉襄國，漳水可溉鄴下，而瀛海當眾河下流，故號河中，視江南澤國不異。 至於山下之泉，地中之水，所在皆有，宜各設壩建閘，通渠築堤，高者自灌，下則車汲。 用南方水田法，六郡之內，得水田數萬頃，畿民從此饒，永無旱澇之患。 不幸濱河有梗，亦可改折於南，取糴於北。 此國家無窮利也。 」報可。 應蛟乃於天津葛沽、何家圈、雙溝、白塘，令防海軍丁屯種，人授田四畝，共種五千餘畝，水稻二千畝，收多，因上言：「墾地七千頃，歲可得穀二百餘萬石，此行之而效者也。」
In year thirty Baoding grand coordinator Wang Yingjiao wrote, "The Yishui could irrigate Jintai, the Hutuo Hengshan, the Tang Zhongshan, the Fu Xiangguo, the Zhang the lands below Ye—and Yinghai, where every river ends, is called River Center; it is no less a water country than the south. Springs on the hillsides and groundwater below are found everywhere; dams and sluices, canals and dikes should be built so high fields can irrigate themselves and low fields be watered by lift. With southern wet-field methods, tens of thousands of mu of paddy could be gained across the six prefectures; the metropolitan people would grow rich and be forever free of drought and flood. If the river route were blocked, tribute grain could be shifted south and provisions drawn from the north. That would be profit without end for the state. The court approved. Yingjiao had coastal-defense troops plant at Tianjin's Geju, Hejiaquan, Shuanggou, and Baitang—four mu per man, more than five thousand mu in all, two thousand mu in rice—with a rich harvest; he reported, "Seven thousand qing reclaimed would yield more than two million shi a year; here is proof the policy works."
83
是年，真定知府郭勉浚大鳴、小鳴泉四十餘穴，溉田千頃。 邢臺達活、野狐二泉流為牛尾河，百泉流為澧河，建二十一閘二堤，灌田五百餘頃。
That year Zhending prefect Guo Mian opened more than forty outlets of the Great and Little Ming springs and irrigated one thousand qing of fields. At Xingtai the Dahu and Yehu springs fed the Niwei River and the Hundred Springs the Li River; twenty-one sluices and two dikes were built to water more than five hundred qing.
84
天啟元年，御史左光鬥用應蛟策，復天津屯田，令通判盧觀象管理屯田水利。 明年，巡按御史張慎言言：「自枝河而西，靜海、興濟之間，萬頃沃壤。 河之東，尚有鹽水沽等處為膏腴之田，惜皆蕪廢。 今觀象開寇家口以南田三千餘畝，溝洫蘆塘之法，種植疏浚之方，皆具而有法，人何憚而不為？ 大抵開種之法有五：一官種。 謂牛、種、器具、耕作、僱募皆出於官，而官亦盡收其田之入也。 一佃種。 謂民願墾而無力，其牛、種、器具仰給於官，待納稼之時，官十而取其四也。 一民種。 佃之有力者，自認開墾若干，迨開荒既熟，較數歲之中以為常，十一而取是也。 一軍種。 即令海防營軍種葛沽之田，人耕四畝，收二石，緣有行、月糧，故收租重也。 一屯種。 祖宗衛軍有屯田，或五十畝，或百畝。 軍為屯種者，歲入十七於官，即以所入為官軍歲支之用。 國初兵農之善制也。 四法已行，惟屯種則今日兵與軍分，而屯僅存其名。 當選各衛之屯餘，墾津門之沃土，如官種法行之。 」章下所司，命太僕卿董應舉管天津至山海屯田，規畫數年，開田十八萬畝，積穀無算。
In Tianqi year one censor Zuo Guangdou revived Yingjiao's scheme, restored Tianjin garrison fields, and put vice prefect Lu Guanxiang in charge of their irrigation. The next year investigating censor Zhang Shenyan wrote, "West of the branch channel, between Jinghai and Xingji, lies ten thousand qing of rich soil. East of the river, Yanshui Gu and the like remain fertile ground—yet all lie abandoned. Guanxiang has already opened more than three thousand mu south of Koujiakou with full methods for ditches, reed ponds, planting, and dredging—what keeps people from following suit? Opening land, in brief, follows five methods. First, official planting. The state supplies oxen, seed, tools, plowing, and hired labor and takes the entire harvest. Second, tenant planting. Peasants who wish to reclaim but lack means receive oxen, seed, and tools from the state and pay four-tenths of the harvest at harvest time. Third, civilian planting. Stronger tenants pledge to open a set acreage; once the wasteland bears, a tithe is taken based on several years' average yield. Fourth, military planting. Coastal-defense troops plant the Geju fields—four mu per man, two shi harvested—and because they still draw travel pay and monthly grain, the rent is heavier. Fifth, garrison planting. The founding guard troops held garrison fields of fifty or one hundred mu each. Soldiers on garrison duty paid seventeen parts of the yield to the state, which funded the troops' annual pay. It was the founding era's fine union of army and agriculture. Four of these methods are already in use; only garrison planting survives in name, for soldiers and garrison troops are now separate. Surplus garrison land from the guards should be chosen to reclaim Tianjin's rich soil under the official-planting method. The memorial went to the responsible offices; the emperor ordered Grand Steward Dong Yingju to oversee garrison fields from Tianjin to Shanhai. Over several years he opened one hundred eighty thousand mu and amassed grain beyond counting.
85
崇禎二年，兵部侍郎申用懋言：「永平濼河諸水，逶迤寬衍，可疏渠以防旱潦。 山坡隙地，便栽種。 宜令有司相地察源，為民興利。 」從之。
In Chongzhen year two Vice Minister of War Shen Yongmao wrote, "The Luo River and other streams of Yongping wind wide and far; canals could be cut to guard against drought and flood. Slopes and pockets of ground are fit for planting. Officials should be ordered to survey the terrain, trace the water sources, and bring the people real benefit. The proposal was approved.
